correctness.rationale: Every connected-set simplex contributes its highest-ranked coordinate vertex. An adjacent label swap affects exactly connected sets containing both swapped labels and avoiding earlier-ranked labels; all weights are strictly positive and contributions point in the same \(e_u-e_v\) direction. In a tree, such a set exists exactly when all \(d-1\) internal vertices of the unique u–v path follow the adjacent block. Contracting the pair yields a uniform permutation of \(n-1\) objects in which the block precedes those \(d-1\) path vertices with probability \(1/d\). Since there are (n-1)! undirected permutohedral edges carrying that pair, exactly \((n-1)!/d\) survive. This proves labelled metric recovery, the Harary index sum, and star/path fractions for all \(n\ge2\). The separate direct-exposure standard-library checker enumerates all 145 labelled trees of order \(\le5\) and 6 selected larger trees, 151 exact passes. The checker is finite corroboration, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: A natural geometric statistic of adjacent braid chambers reconstructs the full labelled graph distance matrix of any tree from a generalized permutahedron fan, and works for every positive connected-tube weighting. The aggregate links a classical global distance invariant to a concrete wall-survival count and yields markedly different asymptotic local sensitivity of path versus star graph associahedra. This is an all-tree structural metric-reconstruction theorem, not merely a renamed Harary index or arbitrary finite numerical gain.
